title: Capacity Sentry & Error‑Budget Forensics Playbook
author: Lena Zhang
content:
Overview
======
This playbook defines the Capacity Sentry pattern: an automated detection-and-forensics workflow that protects SLOs by pairing proactive capacity signals with rapid error‑budget investigation. It combines telemetry contracts, tenant-level headroom guards, and a short evidence collection runbook so oncall can diagnose and remediate model‑inference overloads quickly and consistently.

Who should use this
-------------------
- Model-serving oncall engineers
- SREs owning multi‑tenant capacity orchestration
- Platform PMs and Product SREs defining SLOs and admission policies

Goals
-----
- Detect cross‑tenant model overloads and asymmetric burst behavior within 60s of onset.
- Provide a standard evidence bundle for every SLO incident (telemetry, sample requests, KV cache heatmap).
- Automate pre‑emptive soft‑eviction or throttling to preserve high‑priority tenant SLOs while keeping the control plane responsive.

Key concepts and definitions
---------------------------
- Capacity Sentry: a service that runs anomaly detectors across token headroom, queue length, token consumption rate, and quantized memory pressure and emits alerts with severity tiers (info/warning/critical).
- Headroom: the difference between current allocated compute units and expected 90th percentile demand for the next 10 minutes. Expressed in "GPU units" or relative percentage.
- Error budget forensics bundle: minimal artifact set to capture for postmortem: sampling of 500 requests (or 2 minutes), model variant, quantization profile, kernel mapping, and per-token latency distribution.

SLOs and thresholds (example)
-----------------------------
| Metric                              | Target | Warning threshold | Critical threshold | Notes |
|-------------------------------------|--------|-------------------|--------------------|-------|
| p99 inference latency (serving)     | < 350ms| > 400ms           | > 600ms            | per-tenant, 60s window |
| token loss/errors rate              | < 0.1% | > 0.5%            | > 1.5%             | includes OOM and model falls back |
| token headroom                      | >= 20% | < 15%             | < 8%               | relative to committed capacity |
| queue length (per worker)           | < 4    | >= 10             | >= 25              | backpressure indicator |
| KV cache miss rate                  | < 12%  | >= 25%            | >= 45%             | rapid miss increase indicates churn |

Operational components
----------------------
- Detector microservice (capacity-sentry): emits signals to PagerDuty and Sentry with evidence bundle links.
- Evidence store (immutable): S3 prefix with sampling manifest and telemetry snapshot. TTL: 90 days.
- Admission controller: enforces soft throttles and tenant prioritization policies via the traffic-shaper service.
- Observability dashboards: tenant headroom, per-worker heatmap, model-variant mapping, and emergency throttle panel.

Runbook: immediate steps (oncall)
--------------------------------
1) Acknowledge alert and classify severity (info|warning|critical).
2) Attach the evidence bundle URL from the alert. If missing, run the collector (see CLI below) immediately.
3) Run quick triage queries (PromQL examples):
   - Recent headroom trend: rate(token_headroom[2m]) and headroom_last = token_headroom{tenant="$TENANT"} | topk(1, headroom_last)
   - Latency tail: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[2m])) by (le,tenant))
   - Queue pressure: sum(inflight_requests{tenant="$TENANT"}) by (worker)
4) If evidence shows tenant cold starts or heavy cache churn, execute soft‑eviction for low‑priority tenants: traffic-shaper evict --tenant <id> --policy soft --duration 10m.
5) If OOM patterns are present or worker memory > 90% for 3+ mins, initiate rolling model rollback to last stable variant: modelctl rollback --model <name> --to-version <stable> --grace 30s.
6) Notify Product SRE and Customer Success for impacted tenants (critical only).
7) Create a post-incident ticket using template 'slo-incident-evidence' and preserve evidence bundle.

Evidence collection (collector CLI)
----------------------------------
Use the in-house collector to produce the Error Budget Forensics bundle. Example: 

$ capacity-collector collect --tenant T-12345 --window 120s --max-samples 500 --include-kv-heatmap --out s3://evidence/incident-20270112-T12345.tar.gz

Collector output manifest (required keys)
| key | description |
|-----|-------------|
| manifest.json | pointers to telemetry snapshots and request samples |
| requests.jsonl | up to max-samples of full request/response pairs (redact PII) |
| telemetry.snap | compressed Prometheus snapshot for the window |
| cache-heatmap.png | heatmap image of KV cache occupancy by shard |

Forensics checklist (post-triage)
----------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm whether throttling would have kept high-priority SLOs within limit.
- [ ] Verify sampling shows increased token length or prompt replays.
- [ ] Check kernel selection changes (new kernel may add latency).
- [ ] Confirm whether quantization profile degraded tail latency.
- [ ] Capture timeline: first detection, mitigation start, mitigation end, and traffic return to baseline.

Automated mitigation policies (recommended)
------------------------------------------
1) Warning: automated gentle smoothing (rate-limit 10% of offending tenant traffic) for 5 minutes, and re-evaluate.
2) Critical: automated priority lane shift (move Tier A tenants to reserved capacity) + soft-evict Tier C tenants for 15 minutes.
3) If automated actions fail to reduce critical signals in 3 minutes, escalate to manual runbook steps and oncall.

Telemetry contract (minimal)
---------------------------
Every model-serving service must emit the following labels and metrics every 15s:
- Labels: tenant, model_name, model_variant, quant_profile, worker_id, instance_zone
- Metrics: inference_latency_bucket, inference_errors_total, token_headroom, kv_cache_misses_total, inflight_requests, worker_memory_bytes

SLO evidence format (artifact checklist)
--------------------------------------
- evidence.manifest (JSON)
- prometheus.snapshot (gz)
- requests.jsonl (redacted)
- topology.json (worker->zone mapping)
- throttle-actions.log (if any)

Escalation matrix and paging rules
----------------------------------
- Info/Warning: Page the oncall SRE channel, create internal alert ticket.
- Critical: Trigger PD escalation (Level 1 -> Level 2 after 5m if not ack) and page Product SRE and CS.
- Regulatory customer impact: follow legal/compliance notification checklist (see related_pages).

Incident review standards (post-incident)
----------------------------------------
1) Evidence bundle must be attached to the postmortem within 24 hours.
2) Triage must include: timeline, contributing signals, mitigations attempted, and root cause hypothesis.
3) If automation took action, record decision rationale (why automation invoked override).
4) Run a focused experiment within 7 days to validate the remediation change (shadow traffic or synthetic replay).

Tests and exercises
-------------------
- Quarterly tabletop: simulate a multi-tenant cache-churn event and run through the Sentry pipeline.
- Chaos test: trigger noisy-tenant burst (synthetic tokens) in a canary cluster and assert automation reduces critical alerts within 10 minutes.
- Validation CI: capacity-collector must run on synthetic snapshot server and produce valid manifest (CI gate).

Ownership and contact list
--------------------------
- Capacity Sentry service: team "runtime-capacity" (primary oncall: runtime-capacity@redwood.com)
- Evidence store: infra-storage (sla: 99.9% read availability)
- Traffic shaper: traffic-platform (owner: Maya Singh)

Appendix: example PromQL snippets
--------------------------------
- tenant headroom over 5m: avg_over_time(token_headroom{tenant=~"T-.*"}[5m])
- per-variant p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[2m])) by (le, model_variant))
- KV churn detection: increase(kv_cache_misses_total[1m]) / increase(kv_cache_lookups_total[1m]) > 0.25
